Hawkins County, TN Tax Sales: How to Buy Properties at Auction (2025 Guide)

If you’re thinking about buying tax-delinquent properties in Tennessee, Hawkins County is worth a look. This quiet East Tennessee county offers real estate investment opportunities through public auctions held to recover unpaid property taxes.

In this guide, you’ll find everything you need to know about how the tax sales work in Hawkins County, how to join an auction, and what happens after you win a property.

How Hawkins County Tax Sales Work

Hawkins County holds online tax deed sales through GovEase. These auctions are typically held twice a year, often in August and December. The auctions are open to the public and allow investors to bid on properties with unpaid taxes.

You can bid from anywhere—just register online and link a U.S. bank account before the auction begins.

Hawkins County Tax Sale Details

Step-by-Step: How to Participate in Hawkins County Tax Sales

  1. Register on GovEase
    Create an account and link a valid U.S. bank account.
  2. Research Properties
    Check listings 30 days before the auction. Use the County Assessor’s site to review property details, if available.
  3. Place Bids Online
    Auctions begin at 10:00 AM ET. Place bids in real time.
  4. Pay Through GovEase
    If you win, payment is processed via your linked bank account.
  5. Wait for Court Confirmation
    The Chancery Court must approve the sale before it’s final.
  6. Track the Redemption Period
    The property owner has one year to repay taxes and reclaim the property.
  7. Receive the Tax Deed
    If not redeemed, you’ll receive the deed and take ownership.

Interesting Real Estate Facts About Hawkins County

  • Scenic and Affordable: Hawkins County is known for peaceful mountain views and affordable rural land.
  • Popular for Land Buyers: Large parcels are often bought for recreation or future development.
  • Small Town Markets: Areas like Rogersville and Church Hill have steady real estate activity.
  • Flexible Zoning: Some parts of the county have little zoning, good for mobile or tiny homes.
  • Low Cost of Entry: Starting bids are often much lower than market value.

Attractions and Economy in Hawkins County

  • Outdoor Spaces: Holston River, Cherokee Lake, and area parks are popular for outdoor recreation.
  • Historic Sites: Rogersville is one of the oldest towns in Tennessee.
  • Transport Access: Easy travel via I-81 and U.S. Highway 11W to nearby cities.
  • Local Economy: Driven by agriculture, small businesses, and light manufacturing.
  • Appeal for Remote Buyers: Many investors and retirees look to this area for rural living.

Why Hawkins County Is a Smart Place for Tax Deed Investors

  • Remote Access: Bid from anywhere using GovEase.
  • Market Stability: Small-town real estate tends to be less volatile.
  • Affordable Deals: Properties can sell for far less than their assessed value.
  • Flexible Use: Fewer zoning restrictions can be appealing to creative buyers.

Important Reminders Before Bidding

  • Sales Are Final – No refunds or cancellations after the auction.
  • Properties Are Sold As-Is – You are responsible for checking condition and legal status.
  • Redemption Period – The original owner has up to one year to pay back taxes.
  • Legal Work May Be Needed – Quiet title actions are often required for insurance.
  • Possession Is Delayed – You only gain full ownership after the redemption period.
  • Other Liens Might Exist – Research title and public records before you bid.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

Can I attend the auction in person?
No. Hawkins County auctions are now fully online through GovEase.

Is there a redemption period?
Yes. Property owners have one year after the auction to pay what they owe and reclaim their property.

Can I bid if I don’t live in Tennessee?
Yes. Anyone with a valid U.S. bank account can participate.

What happens if a property is redeemed?
You’ll receive your payment back, but not any costs for improvements or legal work you’ve done.

Can I get title insurance right away?
Not always. Many properties require a quiet title lawsuit before you can insure the deed.

Pro Tips

  • Check each parcel using the GIS and tax records before you bid.
  • Call the Chancery Court for detailed answers about auction rules.
  • Work with a real estate attorney for quiet title or lien issues.
  • Stick to your budget and expect extra costs like clean-up or legal fees.

Final Thoughts

Hawkins County is a great option for tax deed investing, especially if you’re looking for affordable rural land or small-town properties. With the entire process available online and predictable auction dates, it’s an easy place to get started. Just remember: research is everything, and patience is key while waiting out the redemption period.
